title: Run your own review standard first
statement: Before content goes to an outside review, run your own review standard over the exact build being sent, as an adversarial pass split by dimension, and fix what it finds.
example: The first run of a 285-criterion pre-review caught a recurring defect and a 72.5% skew in answer positions.
detail: A reading course ran its own 285-criterion standard as a simulated review before the real one, with agents split by dimension, each attacking its own findings before reporting. The first run caught a recurring defect and a 72.5% answer-position skew, and running it turned the question of readiness into a findings list fixed on the team's own clock. After an outside round's main finding was that the team should review its own work first, the course made the pass binding: nothing goes out without its walk-through harness passing, the full gate and a dimension-split adversarial pass on the exact build being sent.
against: A pre-review is noisy unless it is briefed on what is already settled: an unbriefed simulated review "re-discovers your own decisions and drowns the real gaps" (grade3-reading/.claude/skills/sim-review/SKILL.md, lines 35-36). It does not replace a person's pass: "no submission is exempt on the theory that the machine gate + adversarial pass was sufficient on its own" (grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-6/distilled/08-VERIFICATION-DISCIPLINE.md, lines 360-361).
